trust_decision.summary: The messages REST controller decides whose thread access is checked and on whose behalf read/unread/delete act; at the pinned commit it trusts the client-supplied user_id request parameter for any logged-in user instead of forcing it to the logged-in user unless they hold bp_moderate.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'access arbitrary private message threads via user_id'; get_item_permissions_check is the thread-read permission callback and passes the request user_id to messages_check_thread_access at line 326.

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /buddypress/v2/messages (get_items_permissions_check; refactor to shared helper, was already self-or-moderator)
GET /buddypress/v2/messages/<thread_id>; also reached by PUT and DELETE via update_item_permissions_check (line 552) and delete_item_permissions_check (line 754)
PUT/PATCH /buddypress/v2/messages/<thread_id> (new 404 when message_id not in thread)
get_thread_object helper used by update/delete/create (is_valid -> messages_is_valid_thread, cosmetic)
new private validate_requested_user_id helper; overrides request user_id via set_param so get_item (line 252) and prepare_message_for_response read the forced value

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All changed sites are in src/bp-messages/classes/class-bp-messages-rest-controller.php; the v1 class src/bp-messages/classes/class-bp-rest-messages-endpoint.php:13-18 is only a deprecation stub, not a second implementation.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 route: the starred flag is per-message metadata rather than thread content, and the star/create routes do not declare a user_id argument (src/bp-messages/classes/class-bp-messages-rest-controller.php:98-109), so a solver can argue user_id never applies there.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Moderators (bp_moderate) may legitimately pass user_id to list/read/manage a member's threads, and members with no user_id fall back to themselves; a fix that drops user_id entirely or denies moderators breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: user_id absent or 0 -> fall back to logged-in user (fix.diff:190-193)
user_id of another existing user sent by non-moderator -> overridden to logged-in user (fix.diff:190-193)
user_id sent by moderator -> honoured but must be a thread participant for get_item (fix.diff:98-100)
message_id not belonging to the thread on update -> 404 (fix.diff:129-138)

O7_producer.where: Request user_id is sanitized only by absint in the endpoint args (src/bp-messages/classes/class-bp-messages-rest-controller.php:1169-1175); the fix's state hand-off is set_param inside the permission check (fix.diff:192), not a separate producer.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /messages (create/reply) and PUT /messages/starred/<message_id> responses build is_starred from the unvalidated request user_id, since neither route calls the new helper.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only a starred-status boolean of another user leaks, the routes do not declare user_id, and the advisory names thread access, not starring.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 550 lines from landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: update_starred reading an optional user_id param so moderators can star/unstar on behalf of a member, passed to bp_messages_star_set_action.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every other thread route accepts user_id for moderators and bp_messages_star_set_action already takes a user_id (src/bp-messages/bp-messages-star.php:266); a maintainer aiming for parity would add it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: create_item (reply) accepting user_id to check thread access for a moderator replying as a member.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Mirrors the user_id-for-moderator design of get/update/delete; the permission check already calls messages_check_thread_access with an implicit user.

O9_family: broken access control / IDOR (CWE-639, user-controlled key selects the acting user)
